name: Onan
overview: Onan was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the second-born son of Judah. His role in Scripture is briefly noted without extensive detail beyond his lineage and tribal affiliation. No additional personal notes or character details are provided in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Onan means "powerful, intense" in Hebrew, reflecting a strong and vigorous character. This proper name was not given by God but is recorded in Genesis 38:4, indicating the biblical importance of his identity within Judah's family line.
familyAndRelationships: Onan was the son of Judah and had a son named Bath-shua, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:3. He was also the brother-in-law of Tamar, highlighting his connection within Judah's family. Scripture further notes that Onan was killed by YHVH, indicating divine judgment upon him.
scriptureSignificance: Onan's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his position as Judah's second son and his involvement in the family dynamics surrounding Tamar. His death at the hand of YHVH underscores the seriousness of his actions and God's direct intervention in his life. Through his lineage and divine judgment, Onan's story contributes to the unfolding history of Judah's descendants.
